Theme

saint noun

late Latin

Vulg. Ps. 30 (31), 24: omnēs sānctī ejus (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. saint

sānctus, sānctī m.

noun, second declension

a saint; a woman saint, sāncta

Classically the adjective, holy; the Church’s noun for a saint. As a title, Sānctus Petrus, Saint Peter.

Other words

  • dīvus, dīvī m. — a saint (in humanist Latin)

    noun, second declension · also used · Renaissance · Vives, Exercitātiō 7: trānscurre ad Dīvī Petrī, “run over to St Peter’s”; M-O s.v. saint, citing Vives

    Classically a god or a deified emperor (dīvus Jūlius); the humanists’ word for a saint.

Examples

  • Cōnfiteantur tibi, Domine, omnia opera tua, et sānctī tuī benedīcant tibi.

    Let all your works give thanks to you, Lord, and let your saints bless you.Vulg. Ps. 144 (145), 10

  • cum ad memoriās sānctōrum, sīcut in Āfricā solēbat, pultēs et pānem et merum attulisset atque ab ōstiāriō prohibērētur

    when she had brought porridge, bread and wine to the shrines of the saints, as she used to in Africa, and was stopped by the doorkeeperAug. Conf. 6.2.2

See also icon, martyr, apostle, angel.
